Surface: infra

## Current State

Three checkers implement `_shared/work-record.md`'s spec-shaped-body rule "no unresolved placeholder markers (the two deferral tokens and the ambiguity HTML-comment marker) outside the verbatim `## Original request` section", and none of them distinguishes a marker in authored prose from one inside quoted code:

- `shapeGate` (`plugin/bin/lib/issues/materialize-format.js`): `PLACEHOLDER_RE = /\bTBD\b|\bTODO\b|<!--\s*ambiguity:/` tested against everything before `## Original request` (#1240). This is `/flow`'s materialization hard gate; a hit exits `materialize.js` with `unresolved-placeholder` and Settling points at `/claude-tweaks:specify`.
- `validateShaped` (`plugin/bin/lib/compose-record/compose.js`): a substring loop over `PLACEHOLDER_MARKERS` with the same section exemption, used at compose time.
- The prose rule itself (`_shared/work-record.md`, the spec-shaped-body list), re-run by `/claude-tweaks:backlog refine`'s Step 3.5 body-shape auto-downgrade and the grant gate; `specify/shaping-mode.md` therefore tells shapers never to *mention* the tokens, even in prose.

Harness-health drift records quote the current and proposed CLAUDE.md text verbatim in fenced blocks under `## Deliverables` by construction. When the quoted bullet is the "No implicit deferrals" philosophy line (which ends "…leave a T-O-D-O comment without a corresponding record"), every such record fails the gate although nothing in it is unresolved: observed on plugin 6.114.1, `materialize.js` exit 1 `unresolved-placeholder`, worked around by a logged hand materialization. The same shape recurs for any CLAUDE.md section whose template wording contains the word, and for any record that quotes code or prose containing it.

Tests: `tests/bin-lib/issues/materialize-format.test.js` (`shapeGate` cases including the #1240 exemption and "a genuine marker in an authored section still fails"); `tests/bin-lib/compose-record/` for `validateShaped`.

## Deliverables

- [ ] **One helper, two checkers.** Add `stripCodeSpans(text)` to `plugin/bin/lib/issues/materialize-format.js` (exported): removes fenced blocks (```` ``` ```` and `~~~`, any info string, unclosed fence runs to end of text) and inline code spans (backtick runs of any length, per CommonMark) from the authored text before `PLACEHOLDER_RE` is applied. `validateShaped` in `compose.js` imports and applies the same helper before its marker loop. A bare marker in authored prose still fails in both.
- [ ] **Prose rule and shaping guidance.** `_shared/work-record.md`'s spec-shaped-body bullet gains the clause "or inside a fenced code block / inline code span, which quotes content rather than authoring it". `specify/shaping-mode.md`'s authoring-constraint paragraph is narrowed the same way: a token inside backticks is permitted (it is what the two JS checkers now skip); a prose mention remains forbidden. `refine`'s Step 3.5 and the grant gate cite the rule by reference, so they need no text change; confirm with a grep and edit only if either restates the token list.
- [ ] **Tests.** `materialize-format.test.js`: a Deliverables fence quoting a line with `T-O-D-O` passes; an inline-code `` `T-O-D-O` `` passes; a bare `T-O-D-O` in the same section still fails; an unclosed fence containing the marker passes (fence runs to end of authored text); a marker after a closed fence still fails. Sibling cases in the `validateShaped` suite. The `materialize` CLI case "an unshaped record fails the gate" stays as is.
- [ ] `flow/materialize.md`'s "Materialization hard gate" sentence names the code-span exemption in the same breath as the `## Original request` one.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `shapeGate(body)` returns `{ ok: true }` for a body whose only `T-O-D-O`/`T-B-D` occurrences are inside fenced blocks or inline code spans in authored sections, and `{ ok: false, missing: ['unresolved-placeholder'] }` when a bare marker appears in authored prose in the same body.
2. `validateShaped` agrees with `shapeGate` on every fixture in both suites (a shared fixture module or duplicated literals, either way asserted equal).
3. Every existing case in `materialize-format.test.js` and the `validateShaped` suite passes unchanged, including "a genuine marker in an authored section still fails when an Original request section is also present".
4. `_shared/work-record.md`, `specify/shaping-mode.md`, and `flow/materialize.md` state the exemption once each, and a grep for the token list under `plugin/skills/backlog` shows no third restatement of the token rule.
5. The reported record shape (harness-health drift record quoting the "No implicit deferrals" bullet) materializes with exit 0 in a fixture; quoted in the PR description.
6. `npm test` green.

## Technical Approach

Strip, don't special-case: removing code spans before the regex keeps `PLACEHOLDER_RE` and `PLACEHOLDER_MARKERS` untouched and the exemption identical in both checkers. Handle the unclosed-fence case by treating the run to end-of-text as code (the safer direction: a truncated fence is quoted content, not authored prose). Apply the helper *after* the `## Original request` cut, so the two exemptions compose without interaction.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/materialize-format.js` — `stripCodeSpans`; apply in `shapeGate`; export
- `plugin/bin/lib/compose-record/compose.js` — apply in `validateShaped`
- `plugin/skills/_shared/work-record.md` — spec-shaped-body bullet clause
- `plugin/skills/specify/shaping-mode.md` — narrowed authoring constraint
- `plugin/skills/flow/materialize.md` — hard-gate sentence
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/materialize-format.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/compose-record/*.test.js` — new cases

## Gotchas

- An inline-code span cannot contain its own delimiter run; match backtick runs by length (`` `+ `` opening, same length closing) or a single-backtick `T-O-D-O` inside a double-backtick span is mis-cut.
- `sectionText` and the section-presence checks run on the *unstripped* body; only the placeholder scan sees the stripped text, so a section whose only content is a fenced block still counts as non-empty.
- `_shared/work-record.md`'s rule is also quoted by `capture/SKILL.md`'s born-ready branch; a grep for the token list decides whether that quote needs the clause too (AC 4's sweep).
- The exemption widens the gate; keep the "bare marker after a closed fence still fails" case so a stray `T-O-D-O` cannot hide behind an earlier code block.

## Original request

**Summary:** `shapeGate`'s placeholder scan (`\bTODO\b`) rejects a fully-shaped harness-health drift record because its authored Deliverables section quotes the CLAUDE.md bullet being replaced, and that bullet's own wording says "leave a TODO comment" — the marker is the deliverable, not a placeholder.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `bin/lib/issues/materialize-format.js` (`shapeGate` / `PLACEHOLDER_RE`) — `/flow`'s materialization hard gate

**Repro steps:**
1. Run `/claude-tweaks:harness-health` against a project whose CLAUDE.md Philosophy section carries the pre-#621 "No implicit deferrals" bullet (the one ending "…leave a TODO comment without a corresponding record").
2. Let it file its drift record: the body's `## Deliverables` section contains two fenced blocks — **Current** (the stale bullet, verbatim) and **Proposed** (the template bullet, verbatim); both contain the words "TODO comment". All three required sections are present and non-empty; no `TBD`, no `<!-- ambiguity:` marker anywhere.
3. Dispatch it: `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR=… /claude-tweaks:flow #{n}` → `bin/materialize.js {n} --run-dir …` exits 1 with `unresolved-placeholder`.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: the record passes the gate — the marker word occurs only inside fenced code that quotes the exact text the deliverable replaces, in an authored section; nothing is unresolved.
Actual: `unresolved-placeholder`, exit 1. The build had to override with a logged composer-based materialization (`materialize-format.js`'s own `composeHeader`/`composeFile`) because Settling would point at `/specify`, which cannot remove the word from a correct deliverable. #1240 (closed) and #1633 (open) exempt only the verbatim `## Original request` section, so neither covers a marker inside a fenced/inline code span in an authored section.

**Suggested remedy:** strip fenced code blocks and inline code spans from the authored text before applying `PLACEHOLDER_RE` (a quoted line of text is content, not a placeholder), keep failing on a bare marker in authored prose, and add a regression case whose Deliverables fence quotes a line containing the marker word. Harness-health drift records quote Current/Proposed text by construction, so this shape recurs for every CLAUDE.md section whose template wording mentions TODO.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.114.1

Surface: infra

## Current State

`bin/verify.js` classifies each check's output with `sniffFamily` (`plugin/bin/lib/verify/extract.js`) and parses counts with `parseCounts(text, family)`. Two facts make vitest output unparseable today, and only one of them is the ANSI colour the report names:

1. **The counts path never strips ANSI.** `stripAnsi` exists in `extract.js` (added for #1925's `extractFailingFiles`, whose comment cites this record as the lesson) but is applied only inside `extractFailingFiles`; `sniffFamily`, `parseCounts`, `summaryLine`, and `extractFailingRegion` run on the raw text. A coloured ` FAIL ` or `Tests` line is invisible to the `^FAIL `/`^Tests:` anchors.
2. **Vitest's summary shape is not a recognized family.** `SUMMARY_MARKERS` are jest (`^Tests:.*failed`, `^PASS `/`^FAIL `) and pytest (`^=+ .*(passed|failed).*=+$`); `parseCounts`'s `summary` branch reads only `^Tests:.*$` (colon) or the pytest banner. Vitest prints `Test Files  64 passed (64)` and `Tests  727 passed (727)` — no colon, a `(total)` suffix — so even colour-free vitest output sniffs as `generic` and returns `counts: null`.

`counts: null` is then silent by design at every layer: `report.js` omits the `counts` key (pinned by "counts is omitted from the entry when null"), `verify.js` sets `testCountRegression = null` when `counts.tests` is not a number, and the stdout render prints the CAVEAT line only when a regression object exists. `test/verification.md`'s "Suite-count regression caveat (#881)" section describes the comparison without naming the unparsed case. Neither `run.js` nor `verify.js` sets `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR` on the child.

Observed on plugin 6.114.1 (Windows host, pnpm + Vitest 2.x, colour on without a TTY): `counts: null` on both a 64-file and a 43-file suite across two runs, `testCountRegression: null`, while `tests.log` carried both vitest summary lines under escape codes.

Tests: `tests/bin-lib/verify/extract.test.js` (jest and pytest count fixtures; an ANSI case only for `extractFailingFiles`), `report.test.js`, `count-stamp.test.js`, `cli.test.js`.

## Deliverables

- [ ] **Strip ANSI once, before every parser.** In `verify.js`'s check-result composition (the block that calls `sniffFamily`/`summaryLine`/`extractFailingRegion`/`parseCounts`), pass `stripAnsi(text)` to all four; export `stripAnsi` from `extract.js` if it is not already. `extractFailingFiles` keeps its own call (idempotent). The raw log file stays raw.
- [ ] **Recognize vitest.** Add a vitest marker to `SUMMARY_MARKERS` (`^\s*Test Files\s+\d+ (?:passed|failed)` or `^\s*Tests\s+\d+ (?:passed|failed)`) and a vitest branch in `parseCounts`'s `summary` family that reads the `Tests` line: `(\d+) passed`, `(\d+) failed`, `(\d+) skipped`, and the `\((\d+)\)` total, using the same known-category guard as the jest path (an unknown `(\d+) word` phrase blocks derivation rather than guessing). `Test Files` is never used for `counts.tests`; the `Tests` line is.
- [ ] **Belt and braces on colour.** `run.js` spawns the child with `NO_COLOR=1` and `FORCE_COLOR=0` merged into `process.env` (caller values win if already set), so well-behaved runners emit plain text; stripping stays authoritative for runners that ignore both.
- [ ] **Never disable the comparison silently.** When a `tests` check ran, a count stamp is in play, and `counts` parsed `null`, the report entry gains `countsUnparsed: { family }` and the stdout render prints one line in the CAVEAT shape: `CAVEAT: tests counts unparsed (family {family}) — count-stamp comparison skipped; see {logPath}`. `report.testCountRegression` stays `null`. `test/verification.md`'s "Suite-count regression caveat" section gains one sentence naming this line.
- [ ] **Tests.** `extract.test.js`: vitest fixture (coloured and plain) sniffs `summary` and parses `{tests: 727, pass: 727, fail: 0}`; a vitest line with `| 3 failed` parses `fail: 3`; a jest fixture wrapped in ANSI still parses. `report.test.js`: `countsUnparsed` present when set, omitted otherwise. `cli.test.js`: stdout carries the new CAVEAT line for an unparseable `tests` check under `--count-stamp`, and not when counts parse. `run.test.js`: child env carries `NO_COLOR=1`/`FORCE_COLOR=0` without overriding caller-set values.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `parseCounts(stripAnsi(VITEST_COLOURED), sniffFamily(stripAnsi(VITEST_COLOURED)))` returns `{tests: 727, pass: 727, fail: 0}` for the reported output shape; the plain-text equivalent returns the same.
2. Existing jest, pytest, and TAP count fixtures return byte-identical results; the "never a guess" null cases stay null.
3. `node bin/verify.js --count-stamp {p} --cmd tests="{vitest cmd}"` run twice records `checks.tests.counts.tests` both times and prints the drop CAVEAT when the second run's count is lower (fixture-driven in `cli.test.js`).
4. An unparseable `tests` check under a count stamp prints the `CAVEAT: tests counts unparsed` line and sets `countsUnparsed` in `report.json`; no line appears when counts parse or when no stamp is in play.
5. The child process env includes `NO_COLOR=1` and `FORCE_COLOR=0` unless the caller set either.
6. `npm test` green; every existing case in `tests/bin-lib/verify/*` passes unchanged.

## Technical Approach

Strip at the boundary, once, so no parser needs to know about colour; add the vitest shape as a third summary dialect beside jest and pytest rather than loosening the jest regex (a colon-less `Tests` line must not be confused with a TAP `# tests` block — TAP precedence in `sniffFamily` is pinned). Keep counts fail-toward-absence (#892's rule): the new caveat line makes absence visible; it never fabricates a number.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/extract.js` — vitest marker + `parseCounts` branch; export `stripAnsi`
- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — strip before the four parsers; `countsUnparsed`; render the caveat line
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/run.js` — child env `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR`
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/report.js` — carry `countsUnparsed` into the entry
- `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` — one sentence under "Suite-count regression caveat (#881)"
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/extract.test.js`, `report.test.js`, `cli.test.js`, `run.test.js` — new cases

## Gotchas

- `ANSI_RE` is ESC-anchored on purpose (a literal `[1m` in test output is not a code); keep it, do not widen to bare bracket sequences.
- Vitest prints `Tests` once but `Test Files` too; only the `Tests` line feeds `counts.tests`, or a 64-file suite would be recorded as 64 tests and the drop detector would fire on the wrong axis.
- `count-stamp.js`'s regression compares `previous.tests` to `current.tests` only; the vitest branch must fill `tests` from the parenthesized total when present, else `pass + fail`, matching the jest path's convention.
- Some CI images honour `FORCE_COLOR=1` from the runner's own config over `NO_COLOR`; that is why stripping, not the env, is the fix the acceptance criteria test.

## Original request

**Summary:** `bin/verify.js` records `counts: null` for a `tests` check whose output is vitest's default colour-coded summary (`Tests  64 passed (64)` wrapped in ANSI escape sequences), which silently disables the `--count-stamp` regression comparison the runner documents.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `bin/verify.js` (the `tests` summary parser; `_shared`/`test/verification.md`'s "Suite-count regression caveat")

**Repro steps:**
1. In a project whose test command is Vitest (^2.x) with default reporter and colour on (a normal TTY-less `pnpm test` still emits ANSI colour codes on this Windows host), run `node bin/verify.js --count-stamp <path> --cmd tests="pnpm --filter <pkg> test"` twice.
2. Read `report.json` after each run.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: `checks.tests.counts.tests` holds the parsed total (64 test files / N tests here), and the second run compares it against the stamp so a drop would print the documented `CAVEAT:` line.
Actual: `checks.tests.counts` is `null` on both runs (observed twice in one session, on both a core suite of 64 files and a web suite of 43 files), `testCountRegression` is `null`, and no caveat could ever fire — while the raw `tests.log` plainly contains `Test Files  64 passed (64)` / `Tests  727 passed (727)` once ANSI sequences are stripped. The parser appears to match the summary line only when it is free of escape codes.

Suggested fix: strip `\x1b\[[0-9;]*m` before applying the summary regexes (or run the child with `NO_COLOR=1`/`FORCE_COLOR=0` in its env), and surface `counts: null` on a `tests` check as its own visible line rather than silently disabling the comparison.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.114.1

Surface: infra

## Current State
`bin/lib/wrap-up/state.js`'s `readState` derives push status from the configured upstream only: it runs `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}`, and when that fails it sets `upstream: null` and `pushed: false` — the comment reads "Absent an upstream there is nowhere for the work to have gone, so it is unpushed". `bin/lib/wrap-up/render.js` then prints `{head} — {commits}, UNPUSHED (no upstream)`, and `bin/wrap-up-state.js` uses `state.upstream` to pick which reflog to read. That premise is false for every `pr-first` run: `_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`'s Step 2 and `_shared/git-discipline.md`'s phase-exit push use `git push origin {branch}` with no `-u`, so `@{u}` stays unset (or, since #1860, points at the branch-off point `origin/main` when the worktree was created with `-b {branch} origin/main`) while `refs/remotes/origin/{branch}` is up to date after every push. The State block that `wrap-up/summary-template.md` says to render verbatim therefore claims UNPUSHED for work that origin already holds, and the reporter had to run `git branch --set-upstream-to` by hand to get a truthful line.

The ref the helper needs is already local: `git push origin {branch}` updates `refs/remotes/origin/{branch}` in the pushing checkout, so no fetch is required to judge a push this run made; a fetch would only matter for pushes made elsewhere, which the wrap-up State block is not asked to cover.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `readState` gains a remote-ref fallback: when `@{u}` is unset, or resolves to a ref other than `origin/{branch}`, it checks `git rev-parse --verify --quiet --end-of-options refs/remotes/origin/{branch}`; when that ref exists, `ahead`/`behind` are computed with `rev-list --left-right --count refs/remotes/origin/{branch}...HEAD` and `pushed` follows the same `ahead === 0` rule. The result carries a new `remoteRef` field (`'origin/{branch}'` or `null`) and a `pushedVia: 'upstream' | 'remote-ref' | null` field; `upstream` keeps reporting the configured `@{u}` (or `null`) unchanged.
- [ ] `render.js` distinguishes the three shapes: `pushed (origin/{branch}; no upstream configured)` when `pushedVia === 'remote-ref'`; the existing `pushed`/`UNPUSHED ({upstream})` lines when `pushedVia === 'upstream'`; `UNPUSHED (no upstream, origin/{branch} absent)` when neither ref exists. The unknown case (`pushed === null`) keeps its current wording.
- [ ] `bin/wrap-up-state.js`'s reflog read uses `state.remoteRef` when `state.upstream` is null, so the concatenated-reflog logic sees the remote-tracking ref's updates too.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/state.test.js` (fake-runner style, beside the three existing `pushed` cases): no upstream + remote ref present + ahead 0 → `pushed: true`, `pushedVia: 'remote-ref'`; no upstream + remote ref present + ahead 2 → `pushed: false`; no upstream + no remote ref → `pushed: false`, `remoteRef: null`; inherited upstream (`origin/main`) + remote ref present → judged by the remote ref, not `@{u}`; existing cases unchanged. `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/render.test.js` pins the three rendered lines.
- [ ] `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/` line (the family-1 sentence that says `state.js` reads branch/upstream/ahead-behind/pushed facts) names the remote-ref fallback in one clause.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. On a branch pushed with `git push origin {branch}` and no upstream configured, `node bin/wrap-up-state.js --since <base>` renders a `pushed` line naming `origin/{branch}`; after one more local commit it renders `UNPUSHED` with the ahead count.
2. On a branch whose `@{u}` is the inherited `origin/main` (the #1860 shape) but whose `refs/remotes/origin/{branch}` matches HEAD, the line reads pushed, not `UNPUSHED (origin/main)`.
3. A branch that was never pushed still renders UNPUSHED, and a failed `rev-list` read under either ref still yields `pushed: null` (unknown), never a definite false.
4. All existing `state.test.js` and `render.test.js` cases pass unmodified; `npm test` is green.

## Technical Approach
Helper-side fallback rather than `-u` on the lifecycle's first push: the fallback fixes the State block for branches pushed by any tool (the record's own second point), needs no change to the three skill files that spell the push command, and does not interact with `hasNoUpstreamYet` in `pre-tool-use.js`, which since #1860 already reads `@{u}` vs `origin/{branch}` and would need re-verification if the lifecycle started setting upstreams. The `--end-of-options` separator before the ref follows the repo's `git` argument rule (#1686's citation).

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/state.js` — `readState` (the `@{u}` read, `ahead`/`behind`, the `pushed` rule and its comment).
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/render.js` — the `UNPUSHED (no upstream)` line and its siblings.
- `plugin/bin/wrap-up-state.js` — `state.upstream` reflog selection.
- `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/state.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/render.test.js` — fake-runner fixtures.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`, `plugin/skills/_shared/git-discipline.md` — read-only: the push form that leaves `@{u}` unset.

## Gotchas
- `git branch --show-current` returns empty on a detached HEAD; the fallback must skip the remote-ref probe when `branch` is null, keeping today's detached-HEAD output.
- A remote named anything other than `origin` is out of scope; the lifecycle pushes to `origin` by contract (`_shared/integration-branch.md`), so hard-code it and say so in the comment rather than parsing `branch.{name}.remote`.
- The ordering rule stays: `pushed` is judged against whichever ref was chosen, never against both; a configured upstream that equals `origin/{branch}` takes precedence and the fallback is not consulted.
- `pushedVia` is additive on the JSON shape `--json` emits (#1930); no existing consumer reads the new field, so the shape change is backward compatible.

## Original request
**Summary:** `wrap-up-state.js --since <base>` rendered `Branch <branch> — 12 commits, UNPUSHED (no upstream)` for a branch whose every commit was already on `origin` (the phase-exit push had just printed `<old>..<new> <branch> -> <branch>`). The pr-first lifecycle pushes with `git push origin {branch}` — never `-u` — so `@{u}` is unset on every pr-first run and the helper's "pushed" judgment is wrong for exactly the runs whose State block the wrap-up summary is told to render verbatim.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `bin/wrap-up-state.js` (push-status derivation), with `skills/_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` Step 2 / `skills/_shared/git-discipline.md`'s phase-exit push as the reason `@{u}` is never set

**Cost this session:** one manual `git branch --set-upstream-to` to make the State block truthful, plus a Verdict line that had to be written from the push output instead of the helper — the opposite of what `summary-template.md` asks for ("never assert it landed from memory").

**Repro steps:**
1. Run any pr-first pipeline (draft PR opened at run start; phases push with `git push origin {branch}`).
2. At wrap-up, run `node bin/wrap-up-state.js --since <merge-base>`.
3. Observe `UNPUSHED (no upstream)` while `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/{branch}` returns the current HEAD sha.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: when `@{u}` is unset, the helper falls back to `refs/remotes/origin/{branch}` (after the fetch it already does, or via `git ls-remote`) and reports pushed/unpushed from that; or the pr-early lifecycle's first push sets the upstream (`-u`) so `@{u}` is meaningful for the rest of the run.
Actual: the helper reports UNPUSHED whenever no upstream is configured, regardless of what origin holds.

**Definition:** Clear — either fix (helper fallback or `-u` on the first push) makes the State block correct; the helper-side fallback also covers branches pushed by tools that never set upstream.

**Plugin version:** 6.114.1

Surface: infra

## Current State

Found during a pre-release whole-branch review. Two independently-merged PRs each shipped their
own Jaccard-similarity tokenizer and threshold constant, with no shared source and no test
importing either exported constant — so a change to one can silently invalidate the other's
tests without either noticing:

- `plugin/bin/lib/coordination.js` (confirmed, line 17, #1980): `SUBSTANCE_SIMILARITY_MIN = 0.4`
  + `SUBSTANCE_STOP_WORDS` (line 22).
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/near-duplicate.js` (confirmed, line 24, #1944):
  `DEFAULT_TITLE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD = 0.5` + `STOP_WORDS` (line 30).

A search of `tests/` for either constant name returns zero hits —
`tests/bin-lib/issues/near-duplicate.test.js:66` hardcodes "0.5" in a test name/reasoning
(`'title similarity below the default 0.5 threshold does not fire'`) instead of importing the
real constant.

## Deliverables

- Decide whether these two similarity checks are conceptually the same primitive (in which case
  consolidate into one shared tokenizer/threshold module both import) or genuinely distinct
  enough to justify separate constants (in which case document why, and have each test import
  its own module's real constant instead of hardcoding the value).
- Update `near-duplicate.test.js` to import `DEFAULT_TITLE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` rather than
  hardcoding 0.5.

## Acceptance Criteria

No test hardcodes either threshold as a bare numeric literal; both are imported from their
source module.

## Technical Approach

Read both modules' full similarity-scoring logic (`coordination.js`'s substance-similarity check
and `near-duplicate.js`'s title-similarity check) to judge whether they're the same primitive
applied to different inputs (substance text vs. titles) or genuinely distinct enough to warrant
separate stop-word lists and thresholds — this is the actual judgment call the Deliverables ask
for, not a mechanical decision this shaping pass can make without reading both algorithms'
full bodies. If consolidating: extract a shared tokenizer/stop-word/threshold module both import,
preserving each call site's own threshold value unless the investigation finds a reason to unify
those too. If keeping them separate: add a one-line comment at each constant's definition site
stating why the two are conceptually distinct, and fix the test regardless — the test-hardcoding
fix (Deliverable 2) applies either way. Update `near-duplicate.test.js:66` to import
`DEFAULT_TITLE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` and interpolate it into the test name/assertion instead of
the bare literal `0.5`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/coordination.js` — `SUBSTANCE_SIMILARITY_MIN`/`SUBSTANCE_STOP_WORDS`, possible
  consolidation target
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/near-duplicate.js` — `DEFAULT_TITLE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD`/`STOP_WORDS`,
  possible consolidation target
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/near-duplicate.test.js` (line 66) — fix the hardcoded `0.5`

## Gotchas

- Per a standing memory in this codebase, similarity scores are normalization-sensitive —
  consolidating the two tokenizers is only safe if their actual normalization behavior (case
  folding, punctuation handling, stop-word removal order) genuinely matches; verify with a
  substitution+diff test before assuming they're interchangeable, not just by reading the
  constant values.
- If consolidating, do not silently change either module's effective threshold — a Jaccard
  score computed by a merged tokenizer can differ from the original even at the "same" nominal
  threshold value if the tokenization itself changes; re-verify both modules' existing test

Two independently-merged PRs each shipped their own Jaccard-similarity tokenizer and threshold constant, with no shared source and no test importing either exported constant — so a change to one can silently invalidate the other's tests without either noticing:

- `plugin/bin/lib/coordination.js` (~line 17, #1980): `SUBSTANCE_SIMILARITY_MIN = 0.4` + `SUBSTANCE_STOP_WORDS`.
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/near-duplicate.js` (~line 24, #1944): `DEFAULT_TITLE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD = 0.5` + `STOP_WORDS`.

## Deliverables
- Decide whether these two similarity checks are conceptually the same primitive (in which case consolidate into one shared tokenizer/threshold module both import) or genuinely distinct enough to justify separate constants (in which case document why, and have each test import its own module's real constant instead of hardcoding the value).

Step 4's edge is still owed, including when no skill names the new file directly — file the graph row under the section for the reader it addresses and say so in the row. #1995's `_shared/dispatch-waiting.md` is the worked case for staying out of `plugin-structure.md` entirely: one `docs/skill-graph.md` row filed under `dispatch` ("cited only from the contract's one-line pointer — no skill names it directly … for want of a section for contract-owned files"), no `plugin-structure.md` edit, ruling narrowed from the plan's first draft at whole-branch review. That is not the only outcome, though: #1926's `_shared/ceremony-profile.md` was added *into* the curated row itself on a review finding ("the curated `_shared` row lists ceremony-profile.md", `399981c52`) — the row's own self-description ("a curated subset … only the fragments worth calling out here") makes whether to fold the new file into that curated list an explicit judgment call each extraction has to make, not a rule that always resolves to "nothing."
```

## Acceptance Criteria

The Gotchas section's absolute claim that a new `_shared/*.md` file never needs a `docs/plugin-structure.md` mention is contradicted by #1926's `_shared/ceremony-profile.md`, which a whole-branch review explicitly required adding to that doc's curated `_shared` row.

Surface: infra

## Current State
Nineteen test files under `tests/` simulate permission failures with `fs.chmodSync` (unreadable or unwritable directories, mode-000 files, permission-denied parents). Under a root-privileged runner (`process.getuid() === 0`, the shape of a sandboxed cloud or CI harness) the kernel ignores mode bits, the simulated denial never happens, and each such assertion fails deterministically. Four tests already guard for this, each with its own inline check: `tests/hooks-worktree-detect.test.js` (`if (process.getuid && process.getuid() === 0) return;`), `tests/curation-judge-stagepath.test.js` (`t.skip('root ignores directory permissions')`), `tests/bin-lib/residue/artifacts.test.js` and `tests/bin-lib/timing/cli.test.js` (`{ skip: process.getuid && process.getuid() === 0 }`). The remaining permission-simulation tests the record lists (`tests/bin-lib/code-health/scope.test.js`, four in `tests/bin-lib/hooks/sweep-shadow.test.js`, the record-worktree write-failure case, `checkRunDirAnchoredOrOutside`'s unreadable-ancestor case, `archiveRunDir`'s unreadable-run-dir case, the stale-PID case) have no guard, and `tests/helpers/` holds only `git-fixtures.js` — there is no shared root predicate, so every new permission test re-derives the check or omits it. CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml`, `ubuntu-latest`) runs as a normal user and never sees the failures; only root sandboxes do.

Three of the sixteen failures the record lists are not permission-related: `tests/impeccable-plugin-contract.test.js` (installed-plugin version pin) and the two whole-file failures `tests/shaping-mode-needs-removal.test.js` and `tests/tidy-needs-worklist-rule.test.js`. All three pass on this checkout as a normal user (20/20 across the three files), so their sandbox failures have an environment cause (an absent or differently-versioned plugin cache in the sandbox) that this record does not reproduce; they are split out below.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `tests/helpers/root.js` exporting `IS_ROOT` (`typeof process.getuid === 'function' && process.getuid() === 0`) and `skipUnderRoot(reason)` → `{ skip: IS_ROOT && reason }` for `node:test`'s options object, so a skipped test renders as skipped with its reason in the TAP output, never as a silent early `return`.
- [ ] Every permission-simulation test (the `chmodSync`-based cases across the nineteen files, including the four already guarded ad hoc) uses the helper; the four inline checks are replaced, and the `hooks-worktree-detect` early-`return` form becomes an explicit skip.
- [ ] A conformance test that scans `tests/**` for `chmodSync(` and asserts each containing test case carries `skipUnderRoot` (or the file imports the helper and every `chmodSync` test is registered with it), so a future permission test cannot land unguarded.
- [ ] `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s `tests/` directory-tree line states the rule: permission-simulation tests skip under root by name, and `npm test` under root is expected to report those skips, not failures.
- [ ] The three non-permission failures are re-filed as one separate record via `/claude-tweaks:capture` (Impeccable version-pin mismatch in a sandbox with a different plugin cache; the two whole-file failures), with the reproduction condition recorded as "sandbox only — passes locally"; this record does not claim to fix them.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `npm test` under a root uid reports every permission-simulation case as skipped with a reason, and none as failed; the same suite as a normal user runs them all (skip count zero).
2. No test file contains an inline `getuid() === 0` check; the helper is the only root predicate under `tests/`.
3. The conformance scan fails on a fixture test that calls `chmodSync` without the helper and passes on the real tree.
4. The Impeccable pin and the two whole-file failures are tracked in their own record and named in this record's closing comment; `npm test` as a normal user stays green.

## Technical Approach
Explicit skip over early return: `node:test`'s `{ skip: reason }` surfaces in the TAP summary and in `verify.js`'s parsed counts, so a root sandbox reads honestly as "N skipped (root)" rather than silently passing fewer assertions — the record's second acceptance point. The helper is a few lines; the work is the sweep across nineteen files, which is why the conformance scan lands with it. Whether to instead require a non-root runner (the record's alternative) is declined: the root sandbox is the cloud harness this project documents in CLAUDE.md's Cloud parity section, so the suite must be honest there.

### Key Files
- `tests/helpers/root.js` — new; `tests/helpers/git-fixtures.js` is the existing precedent for a shared helper.
- `tests/hooks-worktree-detect.test.js`, `tests/curation-judge-stagepath.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/residue/artifacts.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/timing/cli.test.js` — the four ad hoc guards to replace.
- `tests/bin-lib/code-health/scope.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/hooks/sweep-shadow.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js`, `tests/hooks-dispatcher.test.js`, `tests/reconcile.test.js` and the other `chmodSync` files (`grep -rln chmodSync tests`) — the unguarded cases.
- `docs/plugin-structure.md` — the `tests/` line of the directory tree (`Node test files (node --test runner)`).

## Gotchas
- A test that `chmodSync`s to simulate a *readable* state (restoring mode after a fixture) is not a permission-simulation test; the conformance scan should key on tests whose assertion expects a failure, so allow an explicit `// root-safe` marker for the restore-only uses rather than forcing the helper on them.
- Some permission tests also depend on a stale-PID precondition that root trivially satisfies (the hooks server stop case the record names); the helper covers it the same way, but the skip reason should say "root" not "permissions" so the TAP line stays truthful.
- Do not fold the Impeccable pin and whole-file failures into this record's deliverables; they pass locally and need a sandbox reproduction first (Deliverable 5).
- #2010 (verify stamp inert while the suite has pre-existing failures) is the sibling cost of this record in sandboxes: once the skips land, a root sandbox's suite can go green and the stamp becomes meaningful there.

## Original request

Filed while executing headless dispatch build,test for #1224 (run 2026-09-04T161953-record-1224) — 16 pre-existing, deterministic (non-flaky) `npm test` failures observed, confirmed unrelated to #1224's own diff by comparison against unmodified main.

Surface: backend

**Related:** #1235

## Overview

Makes each terminal show its own ports and stops leases from outliving their worktrees. A statusline segment renders the block base for the current cwd; both worktree reapers and the two skill-driven removal sites release the lease after a successful `git worktree remove`. Release failure is logged, never fatal — Unit 1's gc is the backstop.

**Complexity:** Medium
**Estimated tasks:** 6

## Non-Goals

- SessionStart/ensure (Unit 2)
- `/init`
- dev-url-detection
- Changing any reaper eligibility predicate (release runs only after a removal the existing predicate already approved)

## Current State

- `plugin/bin/claude-tweaks-statusline.js` builds `segments = [renderProject, renderModel, renderContext, renderEffort, renderGit, renderRateLimit×2, findActiveSpec, findOpenLedger, renderAccount].filter(...)` joined by `SEPARATOR`; each renderer returns `''`/null when inapplicable; tests in `tests/statusline.test.js` and `tests/install-statusline-wrapper.test.js` (the wrapper source `plugin/bin/lib/statusline-wrapper-source.js` is byte-pinned — do not touch it).
- Reapers: `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-reap.js` `reapWorktrees()` calls `runGit(['worktree','remove', real], root)` (~line 284) and `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js` `reapMerged()` does the same (~line 133); both fail closed and are tested by `tests/hooks-worktree-reap.test.js` and `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/reap-merged.test.js` with frozen fixtures.
- Skill-side removal: `plugin/skills/tidy/scan-procedures.md` line ~154 and `plugin/skills/tidy/SKILL.md` line ~165 (`git -C "{REPO_ROOT}" worktree remove {path}`), and `plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` Section C (worktree teardown, `ExitWorktree` for own cwd).

## Deliverables

- [ ] `renderPorts(cwd, {home})` in `claude-tweaks-statusline.js`: reads the registry degrade-open, finds the lease whose `path` equals the realpath of the git toplevel of `cwd` (walk up to the nearest `.git` file/dir rather than spawning git — the statusline must stay spawn-free beyond what it already does; for a linked worktree the nearest `.git` is a *file* pointing at the real gitdir, not a directory — the toplevel is still the directory containing that `.git` file, not a path derived from the gitdir it points to, and the result must be realpath'd with the exact same normalization Unit 1's `registry.allocate`/`registryPath` uses for `path` — same casing, same symlink resolution — or a leased worktree's segment silently never matches), renders `:{base}` (e.g. `:20010`), `''` when none; inserted after `renderGit`. The registry read (including a present-but-malformed/throwing `readRegistry`, not just a missing `ports` module) is wrapped in one try/catch that degrades to `''` — AC1's "unreadable registry ⇒ byte-identical output" covers both the missing-module and the bad-data case, not just the require.
- [ ] `release(real, {home})` — imported from Unit 1's `plugin/bin/lib/ports/registry.js` (#1791) — call in both reapers immediately after a successful `worktree remove` (rm exit 0), wrapped so a throw is recorded in the result as `portsRelease: 'failed: {msg}'` and never changes the reap outcome. `release` on a path with no lease (not every worktree acquires one — Unit 2/`ensure` is out of scope here) is a no-op that reports nothing, matching #1791 AC6's release contract — this is the common case, not the exceptional one. Use one consistent identifier for the seam across the Deliverable and Technical Approach — the injectable option key is `releasePorts`, defaulting to `release` from `registry.js`; a test's injected spy binds to `releasePorts`, never to a separately-named `release`.
- [ ] `plugin/skills/tidy/scan-procedures.md` + `plugin/skills/tidy/SKILL.md`: one added line each after the `worktree remove` instruction: `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/ports.js" release --path {path}` (best-effort: on failure, print to stderr only — never blocks the finding, and no other visibility surface exists for the skill-side call, unlike the reaper's structured `portsRelease` field).
- [ ] `plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` Section C: the same release line as the step after removal, always with an explicit `--path {path}` flag rather than relying on the CLI's cwd-based default — `release(path)` only needs the path string, not a live process cwd, but the CLI's automatic `--path` default (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of cwd) stops resolving once the worktree directory is gone or the session has `cd`'d out of it. Passing `--path` explicitly removes the ordering dependency: for the own-cwd path, release the captured worktree path either just before or just after `ExitWorktree` — the explicit flag makes both orders equally correct.
- [ ] Tests for each of the above.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Statusline with a registry leasing the test cwd's toplevel renders a `:20010` segment between the git and rate-limit segments; with no registry, no lease, or an unreadable registry, output is byte-identical to today. Includes a linked-worktree fixture (a `.git` file, not directory) proving the toplevel resolution matches the registry's own realpath normalization.
2. `reapWorktrees` on a fixture where removal succeeds calls the injected `releasePorts` spy with the removed realpath; when removal fails, it is not called; when it throws, the reap result is unchanged except for the `portsRelease` note; when the removed path had no lease, it returns its no-op success with no note.
3. Same four cases for `reapMerged`.
4. Prose conformance tests (per the repo's `skill-prose-conformance-tests` skill): the release line is present after each of the three skill-side `worktree remove` sites, and the wrap-up own-cwd ordering (release before `ExitWorktree`) is stated.
5. `tests/install-statusline-wrapper.test.js` still passes unchanged.

## Technical Approach

Statusline reads `registry.readRegistry({home})` from Unit 1 (require the module lazily inside `renderPorts` so a missing module — older wrapper install — degrades to `''`). Reapers import `release` from `plugin/bin/lib/ports/registry.js` with an injectable seam `{ releasePorts = release }` in their options object, mirroring how `runGit` is injected today.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/claude-tweaks-statusline.js` — renderPorts + segment
- `tests/statusline.test.js`
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-reap.js` — release after remove
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js` — release after remove
- `tests/hooks-worktree-reap.test.js`
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/reap-merged.test.js`
- `plugin/skills/tidy/scan-procedures.md` — one line
- `plugin/skills/tidy/SKILL.md` — one line
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` — Section C step
- `tests/ports-release-sites-conformance.test.js` — new prose test

### Package Dependencies

- none

## Gotchas

- `tidy/SKILL.md` (41,216 B) and `tidy/scan-procedures.md` (41,232 B) are already over the 40 KB ceiling `tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/context-cost.test.js` enforces — check how that test currently treats them (allowance or exemption) before adding; if the addition trips it, add the one line and trim an equal number of bytes of redundant prose in the same file rather than skipping the line.
- Reapers fail CLOSED on every predicate — release must sit strictly after the successful removal and must not introduce a new predicate.
- `reap-merged.js` overlaps open #1235 (Related, `needs:decision`); keep the edit to the lines strictly after the successful `worktree remove` call — that scoping is what makes this edit resilient to #1235's own eventual, still-undecided change landing before or after this one.
- The statusline runs on every prompt render — no `execFileSync` for git, no lock acquisition, degrade-open reads only.

## Decision Rationale

See #1791 Decision Rationale.

Surface: backend

## Current State

#647's expand phase shipped per-grant `grants.{bornReady,bornAuthorized}.{granted,reason}` in `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js` (`permittedGrants`), fixing a bug where the flat top-level `reason` string could pair a granted `bornReady` with the other grant's denial text. The flat `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized`/`reason` keys were kept as a transitional twin, with the module header (`bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`, lines ~10-15) recording a removal condition: delete the flat keys at the first release on or after 2026-11-16 (ship date + 3 months, per `policy-deprecations.md`'s dated-backstop shape).

Two skill-text consumers carry a matching read-side fallback, tagged with the same removal condition: `skills/capture/SKILL.md` (line ~144) and `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` (line ~223), both doing `(permitted.grants || {}).bornReady || { granted: permitted.bornReady, reason: permitted.reason }`.

Confirmed at shaping time (2026-08-17): the module header text, both fallback call sites, and `skills/backlog/refine-lanes.md`'s rendered trust-consequence line (`↳ trust: {provenance} / {band} — {verdict}{, {coverage}% coverage}`) all reproduce exactly as described — the trust-table snippet's `bornReady`/`reason` output fields (written to `/tmp/backlog-refine-trust.json`) are genuinely dead: nothing downstream reads or renders them.

The removal date (2026-11-16) has **not** yet passed as of this record's shaping (2026-08-17) — it is roughly three months out. This record documents and prepares the contract phase; it does not authorize building the removal before that date.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Verify, at build time, that the current date is on or after 2026-11-16 (the first release on/after that date) before making any of the changes below. If built before that date, stop without editing anything and report the record as not yet actionable — see Acceptance Criteria #1, a hard gate.
- [ ] Re-run `grep -rn "permittedGrants" skills/ bin/` to confirm every consumer still reads only `grants.*` shapes (no new flat-key consumer introduced since shaping).
- [ ] Remove the flat `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized`/`reason` keys from `permittedGrants`'s return value in `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`, and delete the module-header comment block documenting the now-resolved removal condition.
- [ ] Remove the matching read-side fallback in `skills/capture/SKILL.md` (the `(permitted.grants || {}).bornReady || { granted: permitted.bornReady, reason: permitted.reason }` pattern and its explanatory comment), reading `permitted.grants.bornReady` directly.
- [ ] Remove the matching read-side fallback in `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` (same pattern, same treatment).
- [ ] Drop the dead `bornReady`/`reason` output fields from `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md`'s trust-table snippet (the `node -e` block that writes `/tmp/backlog-refine-trust.json`) — confirmed nothing downstream (`skills/backlog/refine-lanes.md`'s rendered trust-consequence line) reads them.
- [ ] Decide, and record the decision inline as a code/skill-text comment, how to handle the two disclosed conflation residues before deleting the flat keys:
  1. Withheld grants share one reason string today — `grants.bornAuthorized.reason` can carry born-ready's rationale on the human-filed path. Decide whether this stays as-is (the per-grant shape already fixes the *granted*-path pairing bug; the withheld-grant sharing is a separate, lower-severity residue) or gets its own follow-up record.
  2. The granted path's flat `reason` today carries positive rationale text ("class is clean, ceiling is unattended, grant origination opted in") that no per-grant key reproduces. Decide whether to populate that positive rationale into the granted per-grant `reason` field, or record explicitly (in a code comment) that it is intentionally dropped as noise once the grant itself is visible via `granted: true`.
- [ ] Update or remove the flat-key compat tests in the `bin-lib/issues` test suite to match the per-grant-only shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Hard precondition, checked first:** the build only proceeds once the current date is on or after 2026-11-16. A build attempted before that date stops without modifying any file and reports the record as not yet actionable — this is not a normal "build failed" outcome, it is the record's own documented gate.
2. `permittedGrants` (`bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`) returns only the per-grant `grants.{bornReady,bornAuthorized}.{granted,reason}` shape — no flat `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized`/`reason` keys at the top level.
3. No consumer (code or skill text, across `skills/` and `bin/`) reads the flat keys or carries a fallback for them — confirmed via `grep -rn "permittedGrants" skills/ bin/` read against every hit.
4. `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md`'s trust-table snippet no longer computes or emits `bornReady`/`reason` fields.
5. The two conflation-residue decisions are recorded (as a comment near the code they affect, or in this record's own close-out note) — not silently dropped.
6. `npm test` passes with the flat-key compat tests updated or removed.

## Technical Approach

Start with the grep re-verification (Deliverables item 2) — the module header itself calls this out as the first step, since a consumer could have appeared between #647 shipping and this record's execution.

`bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`: delete the flat keys from `permittedGrants`'s two return objects (denied-path and granted-path, around current lines 128-155) and the header comment block (lines 10-15) documenting the removal condition — the condition is satisfied, not evergreen.

`skills/capture/SKILL.md` (~line 144) and `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` (~line 223): drop the `|| { granted: permitted.bornReady, reason: permitted.reason }` fallback half of each destructure, reading `permitted.grants.bornReady` directly; delete the accompanying "older installed build" comment.

`skills/backlog/refine-mode.md`'s trust-table `node -e` block (~lines 219-234): remove `bornReady`/`reason` from the `out[issue.number]` object literal.

Fold the two conflation-residue decisions into the same edit pass — they're small text/comment changes, not separate work.

Grep the `bin-lib/issues` test directory for `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized` flat-key assertions on `permittedGrants`'s return value and update/remove them alongside the source change, in the same commit.

## Gotchas

- **Date gate is load-bearing, not advisory.** This record was shaped on 2026-08-17, roughly three months before the 2026-11-16 backstop. Confirmed by reading `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`'s own module header, which states the removal condition explicitly and cites `policy-deprecations.md`'s dated-backstop shape as precedent for this pattern (see also #628/#629, which apply the same shape to `policy.yml` key retirements). Marking this record `ready` reflects that it is *shaped* and *queued*, not that it is *buildable today* — `/specify` has no mechanism to hold a record out of `ready` pending a future calendar date (only `parked` + `Trigger:` does that, and only `/tidy`/`/wrap-up`/`/reflect`/`/review`'s Defer paths can add it), so this Gotcha and Acceptance Criterion 1 are the only gate. Whoever dispatches this record (`/flow`, `/build`, or a human) must re-check the date before touching code.
- **Information loss is real if the conflation residues are skipped.** Deleting the flat keys without deciding the two residues (the Deliverables item above them) silently drops the granted-path's positive rationale text — no per-grant key reproduces it today. This isn't a formatting nit; a human reading a future trust/grant explanation loses the "why" for a clean grant unless this is deliberately decided and recorded.
- **Verified against live code at shaping time**, not taken on faith from the issue text: read `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js` lines 1-40 (module header and `permittedGrants`), `skills/capture/SKILL.md` line ~144, `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` lines ~203-235, and `skills/backlog/refine-lanes.md` lines ~75-100 (the rendered trust-consequence template, confirming it never references `bornReady`/`reason`). All three deliverables reproduce exactly as the original request states — no false premise to correct here.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s two Task-call templates are asymmetric on report fidelity. The second call (`review,polish,wrap-up`) carries an explicit instruction, right before its `OUTPUT FORMAT` section:

> CRITICAL: your review step must re-derive its verdict from raw artifacts -- the actual diff, the actual test-output log in the run directory -- never from a prior claim, whether that claim lives in conversation ... or in a file the first call wrote (decisions.md, ledger entries, staged proposals). Treat every such file's claims as unverified until checked against the artifact it claims to summarize.

with a concrete artifact reference immediately after it (`verify.js --stamp-status`/`report.json` via `bin/lib/dispatch/artifact-verdict.js`'s `deriveTestVerdict`). The first call (`build,test`) has no equivalent instruction anywhere in its own fenced template — it goes straight from the ephemeral-dev-server note to `OUTPUT FORMAT (required)` with nothing between that requires its own `DONE`/`build-test-ok` claim to be checked against an actual artifact before being reported.

This asymmetry produced a real incident this session: a first-call report claimed "5/5 clean under load" with no supporting artifact in the run directory. It surfaced only because an unrelated sibling agent's own discrepancy report prompted the orchestrator to demand reconciliation — nothing in the first call's own template would have caught it otherwise. Measured this session: 2 of roughly 24 dispatched build/review reports (~8%) were later found unsupported or incomplete by independent re-verification.

## Deliverables

- Add a `CRITICAL` instruction to the first call's fenced template in `dispatch/task-prompt.md`, structurally mirroring the second call's (same wording pattern, same placement — immediately before `OUTPUT FORMAT (required)`): the first call's own `DONE`/`build-test-ok` claim must be backed by an actual artifact existing in the run directory at report time (the test-output log / `verify.js --stamp-status` + `report.json`, or whichever artifact the underlying `/claude-tweaks:flow build,test` invocation actually wrote), never asserted from narrative or memory of an earlier pass.
- Keep the instruction's scope accurate to what's different about the first call: unlike the second call (which distrusts a *prior* call's claim), the first call IS the producer — so the instruction should read as "confirm your own claim against the artifact you just produced," not copy the second call's "never trust a prior claim" framing verbatim where it doesn't fit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s first-call fenced template contains a `CRITICAL` instruction, placed immediately before its `OUTPUT FORMAT (required)` section, requiring the reported `OUTCOME`/`STATUS` to be checked against an actual artifact rather than asserted.
- [ ] The added instruction is worded for the first-call's own role (self-verification of a freshly produced claim), not a verbatim copy of the second call's prior-claim-distrust wording.
- [ ] A prose-conformance test (mirroring the pattern the repo already uses for pinning skill prose, e.g. `tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js`'s style) asserts both templates carry a `CRITICAL` re-derive-from-artifacts instruction, so a future edit to either can't silently drop it behind a green suite.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Edit `plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s "## First call — build,test" fenced block, inserting a new paragraph directly before the existing `OUTPUT FORMAT (required)` line — the same position the second call's own `CRITICAL` paragraph occupies relative to its `OUTPUT FORMAT` line. Model the wording on the second call's instruction (`## Second call` section, the paragraph beginning "CRITICAL: your review step must re-derive its verdict from raw artifacts") but adapt the framing: the first call has no *prior* call's claim to distrust — it's confirming its own freshly-produced result — so phrase it as requiring the actual test-output artifact to exist and match before the call reports `DONE`/`build-test-ok`, rather than reusing "never trust a prior claim." Then add or extend a prose-conformance test asserting both call templates carry this instruction (grep for the literal `CRITICAL:` + an artifact-reference phrase in each fenced block), following the existing `tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js` pattern for pinning prose against a live corpus.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md` — add the `CRITICAL` instruction to the first call's fenced template
- `tests/` — new or extended prose-conformance test pinning both templates' `CRITICAL` instructions

## Gotchas

- Don't copy the second call's wording verbatim — it's phrased around distrusting a *prior* call's claim, which doesn't apply to the first call (it has no prior call in this pipeline run). Adapt the framing to self-verification of a freshly produced claim.
- This is a prose-only change to a Task-dispatch prompt template — there's no runtime code path to unit-test directly; the prose-conformance test is what pins the actual instruction text against regression, per this repo's own established pattern for this class of change.

## Original request

dispatch/task-prompt.md: first build,test call has no re-derive-from-artifacts check before reporting DONE

**Summary:** `dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s first (`build,test`) Task-call template has no requirement to re-derive its own claims from actual artifacts before reporting `DONE`, unlike the second (`review`) call, which produced at least one unsupported "all clean" report this session.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** dispatch/task-prompt.md (first-call `build,test` template)

**Objective:** Report fidelity

**Repro steps:**
1. Dispatch a group's first Task call (`build,test`) per `dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s first template.
2. Have it report a verification claim (e.g. "5/5 clean under load") without the underlying artifact actually existing in the run directory, or with a stale/incomplete premise inherited from an earlier record's own already-merged fix.
3. Note that the second (`review`) call's template explicitly instructs "re-derive your verdict from raw artifacts, never trust a prior claim" — but no equivalent instruction applies to the first call before *it* reports `DONE` in the first place.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: a `DONE` status line from the first call implies its own claims are backed by artifacts that actually exist at the time it's reported.
Actual: one first-call report this session claimed "5/5 clean" verification with no supporting artifact in the run directory. It was caught only because an unrelated sibling agent's own discrepancy report prompted the orchestrator to explicitly demand reconciliation before trusting it — nothing in the first call's own template would have caught it otherwise.

**Measurement:** 2 of roughly 24 dispatched build/review reports this session were later found unsupported or incomplete by independent re-verification (~8%).

**Cost this session:** One full re-verification cycle, plus one corrective follow-up fix to an already-merged record's own claim, that would not have happened without an orchestrator or peer agent independently checking rather than trusting the narrative.

**Proposed fix:** Give the first-call template the same "re-derive from raw artifacts before claiming DONE" instruction the second call already carries, rather than deferring all verification skepticism to the second call.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.118.0

Surface: infra

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js`'s `resolveParent()` (line 392) resolves a record's decomposition parent with `gh issue view {n} --json parent`. On `gh` 2.92.0 (2026-04-28) that field is not in the command's JSON field list, the call throws `Unknown JSON field: "parent"`, and `resolveParent` returns `{ok: false}` — which the `acceptance-labeling` check folds into a `fail` row, so `wrap-up-engine.js verify` exits 3 and `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up`'s Verify step withholds the closure line (`execution-and-verification.md`'s exit-3 rule) on every record-mode run, even when the record's `demo:*` labeling is correct. On `gh` 2.96.0 (this checkout, 2026-09-09) the same command returns `{"parent": null}`, so the failure is version-dependent: any sandbox or machine still on 2.92.x hits it on every run.

Two things are wrong at once. The field choice is fragile — the plugin's other parent/sub-issue resolution (`bin/lib/issues/native-dependencies.js`, `fetchNativeSubIssues`) goes through GraphQL, which exposes `Issue.parent` on every `gh` version that can run GraphQL at all. And the failure class is misreported — every other gather failure in this file (`git status`, `git worktree list`, `git log`, `gh pr view`, lines 172–326) renders `result: 'unknown'`, which the closure line quotes without blocking, while `resolveParent`'s failure alone is rendered as `fail`, turning a tooling gap into a false labeling verdict.

## Deliverables

- Resolve the parent through GraphQL — `gh api graphql` with `repository(owner,name){ issue(number){ parent { number } } }` — through the same `deps.gh` seam the rest of the file uses, so the test double can drive it; keep the resolution in `resolveParent` (or a sibling in `native-dependencies.js` it delegates to) and drop the `--json parent` call.
- When the parent gather itself fails (GraphQL error, unparseable response), render the `acceptance-labeling` row as `result: 'unknown'` with the gather error in `detail`, matching the file's other could-not-gather rows — never `fail`. A real labeling mismatch on a successfully resolved record stays `fail`.
- Extend `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.test.js`: a record whose `deps.gh` GraphQL call returns a parent redirects the labeling check to the parent; a null parent takes the non-parent path; a throwing gather renders `unknown` and does not set exit 3.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `resolveParent` no longer invokes `gh issue view … --json parent`; `grep -n "'--json', 'parent'" plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` returns nothing.
- With a `deps.gh` double that throws `Unknown JSON field: "parent"` (or any error) on the parent lookup, `verify` renders `| acceptance-labeling | unknown | … |` and exits 0 when every other check passes; the closure line quotes the unknown row per `execution-and-verification.md`.
- With a double that returns a parent number, the check reads labels/comments from the parent record; with `parent: null`, from the record itself — both covered by tests.
- `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Add a `parentOf(n)` GraphQL query beside `fetchNativeSubIssues` in `native-dependencies.js` (same `runner` seam, same `{owner, repo}` resolution) and have `resolveParent` call it via `deps.gh(['api', 'graphql', '-f', query, '-F', …])`. In the `acceptance-labeling` check (line ~463), branch on `resolved.ok`: false → return `{ result: 'unknown', detail: resolved.error }` before any label read. Keep the existing `{ok, error}` return shape so the check's other callers are untouched. Tests use the file's existing `deps` injection; no live `gh`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` — `resolveParent` (GraphQL via `deps.gh`), `acceptance-labeling` check's could-not-gather branch
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/native-dependencies.js` — optional `parentOf` helper sharing the GraphQL runner seam
- `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.test.js` — parent-redirect, null-parent, and gather-failure cases
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/execution-and-verification.md` — only if the `unknown` row's closure-line quoting needs the acceptance-labeling case named explicitly

## Gotchas

- Do not "fix" this by pinning a minimum `gh` version: the field works on 2.96 but the plugin runs in sandboxes that install whatever `gh` the image ships; GraphQL is the version-stable path the plugin already relies on elsewhere.
- `unknown` must stay distinct from `skip` (the file's own comment at line 109); a gather failure is not a deliberately skipped check.
- The `deps.gh` double in `engine-verify.test.js` matches on argv — the GraphQL call's argv shape must be stable enough for the existing matcher style, or add one helper the tests can stub by name.

## Original request

wrap-up verify: acceptance-labeling check fails on every record-mode run — `gh issue view --json parent` is not a valid field in gh 2.92.0

**Summary:** `bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js`'s `resolveParent()` calls `gh issue view {n} --json parent`; `gh` 2.92.0 rejects `parent` as an unknown JSON field, so the `acceptance-labeling` row renders `fail` and `verify` exits 3 for any record-mode run, blocking the closure line even when labeling was correct.

**Kind:** Defect

Mirror the existing `Promise.all` idiom already used in this file (`pack.js:452`) rather than introducing a new pattern.

## Current State

`agent-browser` is a third-party tool this plugin depends on optionally (CLAUDE.md's Dependencies
table) — it is not part of this repo's own codebase; `plugin/skills/browse/agent-browser-reference.md`
documents its usage but does not own its implementation. That reference file's documented operation
vocabulary (open, snapshot, find, click, fill, screenshot, vitals, trace, etc.) has no
color-scheme/emulation flag.

Verifying a light-mode-only CSS change in a project whose theming is driven solely by
`prefers-color-scheme` media queries (no in-app toggle) required building a standalone HTML
fixture with the target CSS rules copied in and the desired scheme's token values inlined, opened
via `file://`, instead of driving the live app in the actual scheme under test — a real but
indirect substitute.

Because `agent-browser` is external, this record's scope is bounded by what this repo can
actually change: whether the tool already supports color-scheme emulation through some mechanism
not yet documented here, and if not, formalizing the documented workaround so a future verifier
doesn't have to rediscover it.

## Deliverables

- Investigate whether the installed `agent-browser` version already supports color-scheme
  emulation via an undocumented flag, environment variable, or underlying CDP passthrough (e.g.
  `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia`) — check its own `--help` output and any bundled documentation
  first.
- If a mechanism already exists: document it in `agent-browser-reference.md`'s operation
  vocabulary, with a usage example.
- If no mechanism exists: document the standalone-HTML-fixture workaround (build a minimal
  fixture with the target CSS and the desired scheme's token values inlined, open via `file://`)
  as the recommended pattern in `agent-browser-reference.md`, so a future verifier facing the same
  gap has a documented path instead of reinventing it — and, separately, file feedback against
  `agent-browser` itself (outside this repo) requesting the capability, since this repo cannot add
  a feature to a tool it doesn't own.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `agent-browser-reference.md` documents either (a) a working color-scheme emulation flag/option,
  verified against the actually-installed tool version, or (b) the standalone-fixture workaround
  pattern, clearly labeled as a workaround rather than a native capability.
- Whichever path is documented is validated by actually using it to verify a light-mode-only (or
  dark-mode-only) CSS change against a real project with `prefers-color-scheme`-only theming —
  not merely described in the abstract.
- If no native mechanism exists, upstream feedback is filed against `agent-browser` (outside this
  repo's own issue tracker) requesting the capability, and that filing is referenced from this
  record's closing comment.

## Technical Approach

Run `agent-browser --help` (and any subcommand-specific help, e.g. `agent-browser open --help`)
against the actually-installed version to check for an existing but undocumented emulation
option before assuming none exists — third-party tools frequently expose CDP-passthrough flags
that aren't surfaced in every doc surface. If nothing surfaces, formalize the fixture-based
workaround already used as a real substitute: a minimal standalone HTML file with the target
CSS rules and the desired scheme's computed token values inlined, opened via `agent-browser open
file://<path>`. Document whichever path is real in `agent-browser-reference.md`'s existing
operation-vocabulary section, in the same format as its other documented operations.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/browse/agent-browser-reference.md` — document the flag (if found) or the
  fixture-workaround pattern (if not)

## Gotchas

- `agent-browser` is a third-party dependency, not part of this repo's own codebase — this
  record cannot add a capability to the tool itself; it can only document what already exists or
  formalize a workaround, plus file upstream feedback if the capability is genuinely absent.
- Don't document a workaround as if it were a native capability — the Acceptance Criteria
  requires the documentation to be honest about which case applies.

## Original request

**Summary:** Verifying a light-mode-only CSS change in a project whose theming is driven solely by `prefers-color-scheme` media queries (no in-app toggle) required building a standalone HTML fixture instead of driving the live app, because agent-browser's documented operation vocabulary has no color-scheme/emulation flag.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** skills/browse (agent-browser-reference.md)

**Use case:** A project ships theming entirely via `prefers-color-scheme` with no manual toggle in the UI. Verifying a change scoped to the non-default color scheme (e.g. light mode when the OS/browser default is dark) requires driving the app in that scheme. `agent-browser`'s documented operation vocabulary (open, snapshot, find, click, fill, screenshot, vitals, trace, etc. per agent-browser-reference.md) has no color-scheme emulation option, so the only available workaround is building a standalone HTML fixture with the target CSS rules copied in and the desired scheme's token values inlined, then opening it via `file://` — a real but indirect substitute for driving the live app in the actual scheme under test.

Surface: infra

## Current State

Found during a pre-release whole-branch review of `tests/bin-lib/issues/shipped-candidate.test.js`.
The test named "no Key Files section and no title match can never classify strong" only asserts
`tier === 'weak'`; it never covers the module's stated "never upgrades a tier on missing data"
rule (confirmed, `shipped-candidate.js:27`'s comment: "a PR absent from this map is simply 'files
not fetched for it,' which the files-based strong signal treats the same as 'files don't cover
everything' — it never upgrades a tier on missing data"). No existing test supplies a record with
Key Files, no title match, and no `prFiles` entry at all — the actual missing-data path the
comment describes.

## Deliverables

Add a test case supplying a record with a Key Files section, no title match, and no `prFiles`
entry, asserting the module does not upgrade the tier on that missing data.

## Acceptance Criteria

The new test fails if the missing-data guard is removed from `shipped-candidate.js`, proving it
actually exercises the rule.

## Technical Approach

Add a test case to `tests/bin-lib/issues/shipped-candidate.test.js`, alongside the existing "no
Key Files section and no title match can never classify strong" test, using a record that DOES
carry a `### Key Files` section (unlike the existing test) but whose corresponding PR number has
no entry in `opts.prFiles` — asserting the result stays `tier: 'weak'`, not `'strong'`, proving
the missing-`prFiles`-entry path is treated as "files don't cover everything" rather than
silently upgrading. Verify the test actually discriminates per the Acceptance Criteria: comment
out or bypass the missing-data guard in `shipped-candidate.js` locally and confirm the new test
fails, before considering it done.

### Key Files

- `tests/bin-lib/issues/shipped-candidate.test.js` — add the missing-`prFiles`-entry test case
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/shipped-candidate.js` (line ~27, read-only reference) — the rule being
  tested

## Gotchas

- The test must supply a record that genuinely has a `### Key Files` section (the existing
  no-Key-Files test doesn't exercise this path at all) — the distinguishing setup is Key Files
  present + no title match + no `prFiles` entry, not merely "no `prFiles` entry" alone.
- Per this record's own Acceptance Criteria, verify the test discriminates by temporarily
  removing the guard and confirming a failure — don't skip this verification step.

No existing test supplies a record with Key Files, no title match, and no prFiles entry at all — the actual missing-data path the comment describes.
